extracted.subtask_description: Short periodical essays (The Spectator) offering moral, aesthetic, and practical judgments about literature, painting, translation, and conduct for a general educated readership. Includes commentary, examples, and occasional translations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation of ancient compositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Compositions of the Ancients... are extremely difficult to render into another Tongue, so as the Beauties of the Original may not appear weak and faded in the Translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid introducing 'unnatural Witticisms' to please ordinary readers; aim to preserve the original's beauties and structural perfection rather than adapting for contemporary taste. Translator should beware that ancients lacking modern witticisms require delicate handling to avoid making the translation 'weak and faded.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Ode structure as a model of perfection
rubrics_metrics.description: An eminent Greek Critick inserted Sappho's Ode entire in his Works, as a Pattern of Perfection in the Structure of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value and preserve formal structural qualities (balance, unity, pattern) when judging or translating odes; structural elegance is a criterion of excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Painting should instruct manners
rubrics_metrics.description: The Art of Painting is made so little Use of to the Improvement of our Manners... What strong Images of Virtue and Humanity might we not expect would be instilled into the Mind from the Labours of the Pencil?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer paintings that represent virtuous or instructive real-life actions rather than merely mythological or erotic subjects; good history-pieces should give an 'instructive Lecture' and move the viewer to noble sentiments (piety, compassion, contempt of this world).

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of subject in painting
rubrics_metrics.description: There needs no other Proof of this Truth, than the Testimony of every reasonable Creature who has seen the Cartons in Her Majesty's Gallery at Hampton--Court: These are Representations of no less Actions than those of our Blessed Saviour and his Apostles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge paintings favorably when they take religious/historical subjects that display complex moral emotions and instructive scenes (examples: Raphael's cartoons illustrating biblical events). Avoid valuing works that merely display languishing nymphs or sleeping cupids as morally instructive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rendering passion in painting
rubrics_metrics.description: The heavenly Apostles appear acting these great Things, with a deep Sense of the Infirmities which they relieve, but no Value of themselves who administer to their Weakness... The Figures of the Eleven Apostles are all in the same Passion of Admiration, but discover it differently according to their Characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate painters by their ability to render nuanced passions and varied temperaments within a scene so viewers perceive moral and psychological complexity; the painter's imagination should amplify the action and feeling for instructive effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engravings and dissemination as public good
rubrics_metrics.description: As an Engraver is to the Painter what a Printer is to an Author... it is worthy Her Majesty's Name, that she has encouraged that Noble Artist... to publish these Works of Raphael.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage and patronize engravings/prints of great paintings to make instructive art widely accessible; subscription publication is recommended as a public benefit and civil pride.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patronage: favor modest merit
rubrics_metrics.description: It is certainly the greatest Honour we can do our Country, to distinguish Strangers of Merit who apply to us with Modesty and Diffidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When awarding patronage or encouragement, prefer foreign artists who show modesty; modest behaviour when seeking recognition is a positive sign of merit and should influence patronage decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art-dealer integrity as a factor in purchase
rubrics_metrics.description: Having heard him commended by those who have bought of him heretofore for great Integrity in his Dealing... I fear'd I should lose an Occasion of serving a Man of Worth, in omitting to speak of his Auction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider a dealer's past reputation for honesty when judging the reliability and value of works offered at auction; praise by others may justify recommending or attending a sale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambition judged by its object and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Ambition runs through the whole Species... This Passion indeed, like all others, is frequently perverted to evil and ignoble Purposes... it does accordingly express itself in Acts of Magnanimity or selfish Cunning, as it meets with a good or a weak Understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate ambition by what it is directed toward (public good/virtue vs. selfish gain) and by its results (magnanimity vs. folly or vice). Education and discipline determine whether ambition produces honourable or base effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vanities of appearance as motives for distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: The Desire of Distinction... is not, I think, in any Instance more observable than in the Variety of Outsides and new Appearances, which the modish Part of the World are obliged to provide, in order to make themselves remarkable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat conspicuous dress and eccentric behaviour as signs of a desire for notice rather than intrinsic merit; such outward displays are to be judged skeptically as motives for distinction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avarice in old age as an absurd ambition
rubrics_metrics.description: One very Common, and at the same time the most absurd Ambition that ever shewed it self in Humane Nature, is that which comes upon a Man with Experience and old Age... I mean the Passion for getting Money, exclusive of the Character of the Provident Father...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regard late-life covetousness (seeking money for its own sake) as a moral failing and a departure from generous ambition; signs include affectation of poverty to elicit flattery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretion as selection and suppression of thought
rubrics_metrics.description: The great Difference is that the first knows how to pick and cull his Thoughts for Conversation, by suppressing some, and communicating others; whereas the other lets them all indifferently fly out in Words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value discretion as the ability to regulate what one communicates (especially in conversation), to suppress unfit thoughts and reveal suitable ones; it is a practical virtue that improves use of other talents and social harmony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretion versus cunning
rubrics_metrics.description: Discretion points out the noblest Ends to us, and pursues the most proper and laudable Methods of attaining them: Cunning has only private selfish Aims, and sticks at nothing which may make them succeed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate discretion (long-sighted, public-spirited, ennobling) from cunning (short-sighted, selfish, deceitful). Cunning may succeed temporarily but loses power when detected; discretion commands authority and lasting effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prudence in friendship and conversation
rubrics_metrics.description: Tully has therefore very justly exposed a Precept ... That a Man should live with his Enemy in such a manner, as might leave him room to become his Friend; and with his Friend in such a manner, that if he became his Enemy, it should not be in his Power to hurt him. The latter Part... savours more of Cunning than of Discretion...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise prudence with enemies but do not overly distrust friends to the point of forfeiting the freedoms and pleasures of intimate conversation; discretion should not harden into suspicious cunning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of ridicule as cure for love's extravagance
rubrics_metrics.description: Ridicule, perhaps, is a better Expedient against Love than sober Advice... Hudibras and Don Quixote may be as effectual to cure the Extravagancies of this Passion, as any of the old Philosophers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When addressing foolish romantic passions, consider satirical ridicule and comic exemplars as effective remedies alongside or instead of moralizing counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skepticism about authenticity of ancient manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: It appears to have been a Piece of those Records... As there seem to be in it some Anachronisms and Deviations from the ancient Orthography, I am not wholly satisfied myself that it is authentick...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess purported ancient texts for anachronisms and orthographic deviations; when such signs appear, be cautious and acknowledge possible spuriousness before accepting or publishing.
